instructions: Put the chicken in a large pot and add cold water until it's just covered. Add a pinch of the salt and bring it to a boil over high heat. Let it boil for 1 minute. Grey foam will rise to the top.
Drain the chicken and throw away the water. Rinse the chicken and the pot so no foam is left.
Peel the ginger, slice it into thick coins and smash them lightly with the side of your knife.
Put the chicken back in the pot, breast side down, with the ginger, 1 tsp of the salt and about 9 cups hot water. Bring it to a boil over high heat, then turn it down so it bubbles gently.

Cover and simmer for about 25 minutes. You're cooking it to 165°F in the thickest part of the thigh, so if you have a thermometer, check it there. No thermometer? Pierce the thigh near the bone: the juices should run clear, with no pink.
Lift the chicken into a big bowl of cold water and leave it for 5 minutes. Keep the pot simmering.
Ladle 2 1/2 cups of the stock from the pot into a jug for the rice.
Pull the meat off the bones in big pieces and set it on a plate. Put the bones and skin back in the pot and simmer it uncovered for 40 minutes.
Meanwhile, rinse the 1 1/2 cups rice in a sieve until the water runs mostly clear, and drain it well.

Heat 1 tbsp olive oil in a medium pot over medium heat. Add the rice and stir for about 1 minute, until the grains look glossy. Add 1/2 tsp turmeric and stir for about 30 seconds, until every grain is yellow.

Pour in the 2 1/2 cups stock and bring it to a boil. Cover, turn the heat to low and cook for 15 minutes. Take it off the heat and leave the lid on for 10 minutes. You can also cook it in a rice cooker on the white rice setting.
While the rice cooks, juice the 3 limes. That should be about 6 tbsp.
Slice the onion as thin as you can. Put it in a bowl with 1 cup ice water, 3 tbsp of the lime juice and 1 1/2 tsp of the sugar, and leave it for at least 15 minutes. It loses its sharp bite.
Tear the chicken into thin shreds with your fingers.
In a large bowl, stir the remaining 3 tbsp lime juice with 1 1/2 tsp of the salt and the last 1/2 tsp sugar until they dissolve.
Drain the onion well. Add it and the chicken to the dressing and toss. Leave it for 5 minutes.
Pick the leaves off the Vietnamese coriander. That should be about 1 cup. Toss them into the chicken with 1/2 tsp pepper.
Thinly slice 2 of the scallions. Thinly slice the 2 chilies and put them in a little bowl for the table.
Strain the stock and season it with the rest of the salt, adding a little at a time and tasting as you go. Ladle it into 4 small bowls and scatter the scallions over.
Taste the chicken. If it's flat, add a pinch more salt.
Fluff the rice with a fork and divide it among 4 plates. Pile the chicken on top.
Serve with the bowls of stock, the soy sauce and the chilies on the side.
method_notes: Both poach a whole chicken with ginger, tear the meat by hand, cook the rice in the chicken stock tinted with turmeric, and serve the chicken tossed with onion, lime and Vietnamese coriander. Delightful Plate keeps it simple with ginger and salt in the pot, a lime soaked onion and a bowl of hot stock with each plate; SBS (Luke Nguyen) puts the turmeric, fish sauce and shallots in the poaching water, fries garlic and ginger into the rice and adds a papaya and carrot salad. No version had 20 or more ratings and RecipeTin Eats (the trusted cook for Vietnamese) has no com ga, so the first read version leads. This one follows the lead for 4, takes the rice stock straight after poaching so the rice cooks while the bones simmer, and takes about 1 3/4 hours in all.
